title: Postnikov convergence in the pro-étale derived category
statement:
For every complex $K$ of $\mathcal R$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the map of
complexes

$$
\iota\colon K\to R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\geq-n}K=\operatorname{Cone}\Bigl(\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}K
\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}K\Bigr)[-1],\qquad k\mapsto\bigl((\bar k_n)_n,0\bigr),
$$

where $\bar k_n$ is the image of $k$ in $\tau_{\geq-n}K$, is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text:
Use the good truncations of [def-kun-truncations], with their canonical quotient maps. Put $K_n=\tau_{\geq-n}K$, $P=\prod_{n\in\mathbf N}K_n$, $T((x_n)_n)=(t_n(x_{n+1}))_n$, and $F=\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$. Use the cone and shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: identify a standard shifted-cone pair $(b,a)$ with $(x,y)=(a,-b)$. In degree $q$ the fibre is $(\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}K)^q\oplus(\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}K)^{q-1}$
with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-T)x-dy)$. Since the quotient maps are compatible with
the transitions, $(1-T)((\bar k_n)_n)=(\bar k_n-t_n(\bar k_{n+1}))_n=0$, so $\iota$ is a map
of complexes; composed with the projection to $\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}K$ it is the family of
quotient maps.

The rotated cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is $F\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-T}P\to F[1]$, where $p(x,y)=x$. Its long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] is exact at the middle three terms of
$$H^{q-1}(P)\xrightarrow{1-T}H^{q-1}(P)\to H^q(F)\xrightarrow{H^q(p)}H^q(P)\xrightarrow{1-T}H^q(P).$$
By [det-pe-products-derived], the canonical map $H^r(P)\to\prod_nH^r(K_n)$ is an isomorphism; its $n$th component is $H^r(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, so the $n$th component of $H^r(T)$ is $H^r(t_n)\circ H^r(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})$. Thus the kernel of the last arrow consists precisely of the compatible families, namely $\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)$. Exactness gives
$$0\to\operatorname{coker}(1-T:\prod_nH^{q-1}(K_n)\to\prod_nH^{q-1}(K_n))\to H^q(F)\xrightarrow{\rho_q}\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)\to0,$$
where $\rho_q$ is induced by $p$. In particular the $n$th component of $\rho_q\circ H^q(\iota)$ is $H^q(K\to K_n)$, by step 1.

proof.text: By clause 2 of [det-pe-milnor-sequence], the cokernel in step 2 is $R^1\varprojlim_nH^{q-1}(K_n)$. Clause 2 of [det-pe-left-complete-truncation-tower], in degree $q-1$, makes this term zero, so the short exact sequence in step 2 makes $\rho_q$ an isomorphism. The same clause in degree $q$ says that the map $H^q(K)\to\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)$ induced by the quotient maps is an isomorphism. Step 2 identifies this map with $\rho_q\circ H^q(\iota)$; hence $H^q(\iota)=\rho_q^{-1}\circ(\rho_q\circ H^q(\iota))$ is an isomorphism. This holds for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, so $\iota$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
